name: OCSF
vendor: OCSF project (Linux Foundation), started by AWS and Splunk

foundation.via: A series of LF Projects, LLC, since November 2024

summary: The Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework: an open, vendor-neutral schema for security events and findings, so logs from firewalls, endpoints, identity providers and clouds arrive with the same field names and can be queried and correlated together.
intro: Every security product logs in its own format, so a SIEM or data lake spends much of its effort mapping fields such as “source IP” or “user name” before any rule can run across sources. OCSF defines one schema for that data. It starts from a dictionary of named, typed attributes and builds objects from them, such as `process`, `user`, `device` and `file`. Each event belongs to one event class, such as Process Activity, Authentication, DNS Activity or Detection Finding, and each class sits in one of eight categories: System Activity, Findings, Identity & Access Management, Network Activity, Discovery, Application Activity, Remediation and Unmanned Systems. Numbers identify everything: Process Activity is `class_uid` 1007 in category 1, its Launch activity is `activity_id` 1, and `type_uid` is `class_uid × 100 + activity_id`, here 100701.

Profiles overlay extra attributes across classes when the data exists, such as Host, Cloud, Container, Security Control or, since version 1.8, AI Operation; extensions let a vendor or platform add classes and attributes without changing the core, as the Linux, macOS and Windows extensions do. Every event carries a required `severity_id`, an `observables` array that lifts key values such as IP addresses, hashes or process names into one searchable place, the original record in `raw_data` if wanted, and fields it could not map in `unmapped`. OCSF is a specification and a schema, not a product: version 1.9.0 came out on August 3, 2026, the schema is published under Apache 2.0, and products such as Amazon Security Lake store and exchange data in it.
strengths: One set of field names across vendors, so a detection rule or query written once works on data from many sources
Backed by both sides of the market: started by AWS and Splunk, with security vendors, government agencies and universities among about 200 participating organisations
Extensible without forking: profiles and registered extensions add attributes and classes while the core stays shared
Used as a storage format, not only an interchange format: Amazon Security Lake converts AWS logs to OCSF and keeps them as Parquet in your own S3 buckets
limits: Mapping is still work: each source needs a translation into OCSF classes, and fields that don’t fit end up in `unmapped`

The schema changes every few months (1.7 in November 2025, 1.8 in March 2026, 1.9 in August 2026), and producers and consumers may sit on different versions; Security Lake’s current AWS sources write OCSF 1.1.0
It defines data, not detections: rules still come from your SIEM or a format such as Sigma, which uses its own field taxonomy

Its path to an international standard is unfinished: ITU-T member states backed it in December 2025, but objections to the draft Recommendation were still being raised in Study Group 17 in September 2026

sections.title: The eight categories
sections.intro: A class’s `class_uid` is its category number times 1,000 plus its own number, so every Network Activity class starts with 4. The core schema on GitHub has about 80 event classes.

rows.label: 1 System Activity
values: File System, Process, Module, Kernel and Script Activity; Scheduled Job Activity

rows.label: 2 Findings
values: Detection, Vulnerability, Compliance, Incident and Data Security Finding

rows.label: 3 Identity & Access Management
values: Account Change, Authentication, Authorize Session, Group Management, User Access Management

rows.label: 4 Network Activity
values: Network, HTTP, DNS, SSH, RDP, SMB and Email Activity

rows.label: 5 Discovery
values: Device, User and Software Inventory Info; Cloud Resources Inventory Info; Process and Service Query

rows.label: 6 Application Activity
values: API Activity, Web Resources Activity, Datastore Activity, Application Lifecycle

rows.label: 7 Remediation
values: File, Process and Network Remediation Activity

rows.label: 8 Unmanned Systems
values: Drone Flights Activity, Airborne Broadcast Activity

story: Security teams spent much of their time normalising data: every firewall, endpoint agent and cloud service described the same activity with different field names, so correlating events meant writing and maintaining mappings for each. At Black Hat USA in August 2022, AWS and Splunk announced OCSF to fix that, building on the ICD Schema that Symantec, a division of Broadcom, had developed, with 15 more initial members including Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, IBM Security, Okta, Palo Alto Networks, Rapid7, Salesforce, Trend Micro and Zscaler.

Version 1.0.0 came out in 2023, and on November 19, 2024 OCSF joined the Linux Foundation, announced at its Member Summit; it then had more than 900 contributors from about 200 organisations, and the move put the schema under a neutral body rather than the companies that started it. Minor versions have kept coming every few months: 1.3.0 in August 2024 added classes for software inventory and remediation and an OSINT profile, and 1.8.0 in March 2026 added support for AI operations.

OCSF has also gone to the International Telecommunication Union as draft Recommendation ITU-T X.icd-schemas. According to AWS, ITU member states supported it for ratification in December 2025; Study Group 17 was still discussing objections to the draft in September 2026.

choices.why: AWS and Splunk built on the ICD Schema work done at Symantec, so the project began from an existing security event schema rather than a blank page.

The schema prefers enumerated integers to strings for consistency, so classes, activities and severities are numbers such as `class_uid` and `severity_id`, each with a sibling string for people to read.

choices.choice: Profiles and extensions instead of a monolith
choices.why: Cloud, container and host details apply across many classes, and vendors need their own fields, so both are layered on without changing the core schema.

timeline.text: AWS and Splunk announce OCSF at Black Hat USA in August, with 18 initial organisations
OCSF joins the Linux Foundation on November 19
ITU-T member states back OCSF for ratification as an international standard (December)
Version 1.8.0 adds an AI Operation profile in March; 1.9.0 released on August 3
